Author: Anil Verma Bench: Anil Verma  1  IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  CRA No. 400 of 2023  (RAVI Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH)
 Dated : 20-07-2023  Shri Omprakash Solanki - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Pranay Joshi -PL for the respondent/State.
____________________________________________________________ Heard on I.A. no. 4232/2023 which is an application filed under section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C on behalf of appellant Ravi for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2/ The appellant has been convicted under section 376(1) of IPC and sections 3 read with section 4 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo 10 years R.I with fine of Rs. 5000/- with usual default stipulation.
3/ Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
During trial, he was remained on bail and he has not misused the liberty granted to him.
On the same set of evidence, the trial Court acquitted the appellant from all other charges.
He has been convicted only on the basis of DNA report.
The procedure for taking sample for the purpose of analysis was not proper.

The sample was kept in unsafe condition for huge period,
therefore, the DNA report cannot be relied upon.
There is strong case in favour of the appellant.
Final disposal of the appeal will take considerable long time.
Under these circumstances, he prays that the application be allowed and the remaining jail sentence of the appellant be suspended till final disposal of the appeal.

In support of his contention, he has placed reliance upon the Prakash Nishad alias Kewat Zinak Vs.
State of Maharashtra reported in AIR 2023 SC 2938 and Rahul Vs. State of Delhi, Ministry of Home Affairs and another reported in AIR 2022 SC 5661.
4/

sentences.text: 1 5/ From perusal of the record, it appears that in this case, dead bodies of minor prosecutrix have been recovered from well and it has been gathered that the appellant has committed rape with deceased/prosecutrix- P, due to which, both the prosecutrix committed suicide.

Nathulal (PW-1)
and Ravi (PW-2) have categorically stated against the appellant that he used to talk with his sister /
prosecutrix.
Nathulal also deposed that when both the minor prosecutrix went to forest for collecting woods, at that time, present appellant along with other co-accused persons went there and caught hold of them.

Although sample was sent for chemical analysis after lapse of so many days,
but there is no material irregularities or illegality in the process of taking sample.
The alleged offence is heinous in nature.
Both the citations produced by counsel for the appellant are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
In view of the material evidence available on record against the appellant, this Court is not inclined to grant bail and suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A no. 4232/2023 is hereby dismissed.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.
